That demotion is well-founded here: this is a genuinely short-payload formula, not a hero-tail artefact.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. adjudicationPoints.title: The cohort's only `balanced` / `neither_dominant` value — and it is not the product R6 was written around — ESCALATION
adjudicationPoints.body: R6's reading (b) was drafted with the structurally minimal gloss mask in mind, and the standard names L'Oréal Elsève Glycolic Gloss as its anchor case. On this cohort it fires on a different product entirely. Pantene Molecular Bond Repair's credited segment is AQUA @1, STEARYL ALCOHOL @2, STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @3, CETYL ALCOHOL @4, BIS-AMINOPROPYL DIMETHICONE @5, GLUTAMIC ACID @6 — a bare R1 base plus one amino silicone, with zero humectants and zero lipids above the tail. Clause 1 holds (no protein at any rank), clause 2 holds (the silicone is the only species beyond the baseline), clause 3 holds (nothing above the tail beyond the bare R1 baseline), clause 4 holds vacuously (there is no candidate leg species to outrank). So the value is `balanced` / `neither_dominant`, moving from v0.1's `moisture` at `high` confidence. Meanwhile #11, the anchor case, FAILS clause 4 — its single humectant PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5 outranks the AMODIMETHICONE @6 that establishes clause 2 — and keeps `moisture`. Two things for Nick. First, is a single amino silicone a 'substantive R2 silicone system' for clause 2? If not, this value returns to `moisture` and reading (b) is reached nowhere in the cohort. Second, clause 4's vacuous satisfaction on a formula with no legs at all is arguably the cleanest possible case for reading (b), yet it reads as a technicality; whereas on the anchor case clause 4 blocks the reading on a one-rank difference between a glycol and a silicone. §18 open question 4 asks how often reading (b) is reachable; this run's answer is 'once, and not where expected'.

adjudicationPoints.title: `weight_potential: low` holds on a counting scope §9.2 marks as its own unruled addition — this formula runs two cationics on the full list
adjudicationPoints.body: E4's leanness test requires 'a single cationic species', and §9.2 counts it on the ABOVE-TAIL segment, as it counts every other term in that section. On this record STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @3 is the only S1-family species above the marker, so the conjunct holds — but BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @11 is a second cationic on the full list, demoted only because PARFUM lands early, at rank 7 of 23. The other two conjuncts do not depend on the cut at all: there is no lipid of any class and one silicone at ANY rank. So the whole question is conjunct 3's scope. §9.2's own [judgment call — review] says this in terms: after E4 the three conjuncts are ruled, and 'what remains this standard's addition there is the counting scope — that ‘single cationic species’ is counted on the above-tail segment', listed first in line for the calibration set (§15, §18.2). WHAT NICK DECIDES: nothing today — this is a calibration question, and the value is recorded as the standard produces it, at `moderate` confidence which is exactly the statement that a neighbouring value is reachable on a rule reading. WHAT IS WORTH SEEING NOW: the same caveat attaches to #09 Balea (second and third cationics both tail-side) and NOT to #08 Sante (one cationic on the full list). If the calibration set moves the counting scope to the full list, #07 and #09 return to `moderate` and #08 stays `low`, so two of the cohort's four `low` calls rest on this one unruled cut.
